I decided to go for a solo trek. Last time, I explored 25% of the hill station named Matheran so I decided to see the rest today and I didn't had even 1% clue of what is going to happen today. I was ready to leave for the Kanjurmarg station by 4:40 and I don't know why I booked Uber to the station and it got accepted in no time. I followed him, he was going to tea shop. I reached the tea shop, show him the payment and he was like “Okay Okay, thik hai.”. There was one guy who said something about me like it was positive only but I don't remember. Anyways, I reached the station around 25 min. and waited there for my train early? Yes? Hell No. As I stepped the platform, a train arrives that has stops at Thane. I had almost 0 cash like not 0 but close to it as I use UPI mostly. So I thought I will look for ATM in Thane and will board my train from there. For Mumbaikers only, Also, I thought since Thane is one of the most important station, I should take train to Neral from there. I don't know but I had some gut feeling that this is going to be good. Miracle! I arrived at Thane around 5:12 AM and guess what! A train to Khopoli was waiting to leave Thane at 5:17 AM. I brought a cute red colored mini-towel with me, I started using it. Question: For every experience, you get: What are the biggest things you want to share with everyone?
Answer: 20 Things before I turn 20! Something I want to say before my coming b’ day…. As someone who is going to turn 20 soon, here are 20 tips/learnings/experiences I want to share with y’all… 1. Dress well When you are well dressed, like you have put on clean and ironed clothes, clean shoes with good socks, hair and beard managed well… You automatically start feeling better. 2*. Live today like you are going to die tomorrow Who knows when you are going to die? Just do what you want to do, ask your crush out! plan your dream trip! start your business! start gym! file divorce if things are toxic for long! buy your dream laptop! get that golf membership! do everything you wanna do. Failing > Regret 3. Fkuc Social Media Bubble Whatever you see on social media is 99% fake. Always remember, social media is highlight of people's life, it's not the reflection. The more you use social media, more are the chances of you feeling sad and depressed. 4. No One Cares Everyone has their own struggles, they don't care about you so just don't care about anything and do what you wanna do but it should be ethically good. And wese bhi, Aaj se 100 saal baad, no one is going to remember anything. So better enjoy doing rather than thinking. 5. Prepare For Atleast One Competitive Exam I mean it will give you reality check about many things. 6. Learn Ignoring People Except some 20–25 important people in your life, ignore everyone. (Saying the guy who was scammed 15 days ago🙂 by a random stranger) 7. Make Friends That Can Benefit You After ignoring everyone, be greedy and find people that can help you in long term.. maybe they can help you getting a job later or maybe they join some govt. job, it'll benefit you. 8. Do Not Repeat Mistakes 9. Feed Animals & Homeless People It will make you feel good Saying the guy who recently gave his mess wala pizza to a dog🙂 10 Talk To Parents Daily Just 5 min. of your day is all it takes. 11. Do Not Drink or Smoke Smoking/Drinking doesn't make you look cool. Like pata nahi, what sort of depression these 18–19 YO have in life that they need drugs, matlab kucch bhi. Bro, You are just 18, everything you want is available in your house. So why are you depressed? 12*. Understand Game Theories Like Zero Sum Game No one can scam you once you understand it all. Except when you trust random strangers in New Delhi. 13. Everyone inside home need love, everyone outside home want money. So just behave accordingly. 14. Internet Can Make or Break Your Life You can make money like many solopreneurs or you can lose everything in gambling. 15. Make Every Financial Decisions Keeping Zero Sum Therory in Mind Stock market is cool, but learn basics before burning your wallet. Insurance is cool but check T&Cs before buying one. 16*. Do Not Share Everything With Everyone Not everyone wants you succeed. I can't tell how good life is when no one knows nothing about you, like life is so easy, goals become easy when no one knows about you. 17. Life Is Unfair Who said it is fair? Ask a person on wheelchair how unfair life is? A girl in my college got selected with 6 CPI but a boy with 8.5 CPI didn't even got shortlisted for an internship. Out of 150 students, the boy ranks in top 20 from the top while girl ranks top 20 from the bottom. Company = HUL And it is the best thing about life that it is unfair! And the even more better thing is if you want, you can make it more unfair. 18. Learn Economics (Basics will work) Economics will help you in daily life not Calculus or Electromagnetism. 19. Everything will change Nothing is constant. Your wounds will heal, Your salary will increase. Time will change everything. 20. If you are having mental health problems, you are privileged. In my 20 years of life, I have never seen any financially poor guy saying that he is in depression, he is having anxiety but…. whereas rich teens get panic attacks every night. Seriously? You don't need to pay any bill or tax. You don't need to feed a family of 6. Depression is nothing but result of continuous regret due to procrastination. Bonus : If you want something, find reason why you want it and get obsessed with it. Stop running after politicians, cricketers, actors. Fuck Them, you are not gaining anything from them. Follow good people and stop reading people who post WA screenshots with their nibba nibbis. You ain't getting anything from those shitty people. Question: What did you learn today?
Answer: Pack of noodle as a currency? I got this info from a newsletter (Groww Digest) over my email and it is very interesting. I learnt about jail and the economy inside it. About 0.5% of the entire US population is in jail. One of the highest rates in the world. The US is also one of the few countries that have privately run prisons. Life inside US prisons is tough. Some have watchtowers with signboards that read ‘One Warning Shot Only’. If there is a riot inside the prison and the prisoners refuse to obey the jail guards, they will fire one warning bullet in the air. The next shot will be fired at the prisoners. Some have signboards with ‘No Warning Shots’ written. The prisoners get fixed amounts of time to exercise, be in the open sky, eat, and use the washroom. There are different kinds of prison sentences. Some inmates are in solitary confinement – they are not allowed to socialize with other prisoners. Theft and violence is an ever-present threat to all prisoners. Prisoners can get money by working in prisons or if their families send them. This money can be used to buy things from the canteens (also called commissary). The kind of items sold in these canteens are limited. Snacks, soaps, stationery, and some other basic supplies. Besides this, they do not have any use for cash inside prisons. The prisoners do not have cash in their hands. A register is maintained in the canteens to track their balance. Other than the canteen, not many facilities are available. It is a prison after all. Ramen – similar to cup Maggi – can be bought from jail canteens. This is used as currency. One pack of ramen costs about $0.6. But this one pack of ramen can be used to buy services inside the prison worth a lot more. Therefore, the price of ramen is quite high inside the prison – in the prison economy. Many prisoners do not eat the ramen. They store it. The more ramen boxes you have, the richer you are. All transactions are done using ramen boxes – cleaning, massage, postcard making, etc etc. What happens if prisons ban ramen? Again, trade and economy finds a way. Ramen has not always been the currency. Prisoners used to treat cigarettes as currency. Some time ago, tobacco and cigarettes were banned in most US prisons. Cigarettes never vanished from prisons. But now that they were legally banned, they couldn’t be used openly. This is when most prison economies switched to ramen. Across the world, prisoners use different items as currency. Packaged fish, coffee, and spices – some prisons still use cigarettes. Whenever an item is banned, a new item becomes the currency. A currency needs to have a few properties: should be accepted by others in the economy, should be easy to carry and store, must be in relatively short supply, uniform, and a few other traits. Any item that has these qualities can become currency. That's it. ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Question: How is gravity the weakest fundamental force?
Answer: It is the weakest force but the thing is we do not get that feel of other forces in nature. And when we compare forces, we consider them at sub-atomic levels as the two of four forces have range of less than some fentometers (1 fM = 10^(-15)m) Let's try to compare other forces with gravity. Electromagnetism Gravity is about 10³⁶ times weaker than electromagnetic force. The ratio of the Coulomb force to the Gravitational force between a proton and antiproton is independent of distance and equals about 10³⁶. Strong Nuclear Force The strong nuclear force that binds protons and neutrons in the nucleus is much stronger than gravity. The binding energy of a deuteron (proton + neutron) due to the strong force is about 2.2 MeV, compared to only 0.75 keV for protonium (proton + antiproton) bound by electromagnetism. Weak Nuclear Force Weak nuclear force is responsible for radioactive decay and neutrino interactions. It has very less range (1 fentometer ig) and is reduced to 0 after that and in the zone, it is more impactful than gravity. The thing is we do not interact with 3 forces in our daily life. And when we compare forces between heavy objects like planets, stars, etc. gravity is the strongest force. (Just a meme) That's it. ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Let's discuss how it affect everyone. According to the bill, the bill is applicable on everyone who creates anything on the internet whether in form of Video, Audio, Text, Sign, Images and everything. Question: I'm so insecure about everything. What should I do to overcome this feeling of insecurity?
Answer: I can relate a lot with whoever asked this question… I'm too insecure about everything, and let me share my escape from this insecurity. Before starting, let me talk about Kabir. He got good genetics, 6 feet tall, bornt in a rich family that owns a house in South Bombay, he is intelligent too and quite smart. He was always intelligent, cracked SRCC easily, got a cute girlfriend in DU, did job in Goldman Sachs for 3 years, wrote CAT, did MBA from IIM Bangalore, and got job in Wells Fargo USA and settled with his Girlfriend (future wife) there, did different jobs for 30 years and eventually took retirement and spent his remaining life remote area in San Francisco. Kabir is exactly what all of us want to be. Right? For me, Kabir is not the type of guy I want to be. Infact, I hate Kabir type people. Let's talk about Rohan. Rohan has average or below average looks, 5 feet 8 inches tall, below average in studies, bornt in a poor family in Gorakhpur, UP. He is not that intelligent but loves to face challenges and get obsessed with things. He got 78.6% in class 10. He got obsessed with Medical Sciences and cracked NEET in his 4th attempt after studying from online platforms, he struggled in his graduation but ended up being a doctor. He was rejected 4 times by his wife during college, but he kept trying on her as he was obsessed with her. He only qualified his PG as I said he was not super intelligent. He made decent money, saw every corner of India, treated both poor and rich in his clinic. In short, he saw every aspect of life. Most of us are Rohan or can become Rohan from the next second. But we aspire to become Kabir. Which is good according to you, for me… It is Rohan. Because I don't relate with Kabir. And Rohan has saw every aspect of life. When Kabir and Rohan both turned 70, and their grandchildren asked them their life stories… Who had better stories? . You got the point. Now, coming back to the point, you are insecure… just be obsessed with the thing you want… We can't be Kabir but we can, everyone reading this can definitely be Rohan. Whose life is more interesting? Definitely, it is Rohan. Hope you got my point. Which road is more fun? Foggy or Clear? That's it. ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Question: Did you ever go on an unplanned trip and how did it go?
Answer: Yes. I don't know if i can call this unplanned or not, like it was somewhere in the middle. (This is a long post, so, continue from here only if you have 10–15 min. otherwise it doesn't make sense to left in the middle.) Suddenly, at 12 Midnight, I got a thought of visiting Matheran, a hill station between Mumbai and Pune. This was going to be my first solo trip to anywhere. (Remember that it was expected to be solo trip) I planned something like this… Sleeping : 1 Am. Waking Up : 5 Am Getting Ready : 6 Am Reaching Local station nearest to my college (KanjurMarg) : 6:30 Am Taking a slow local and reaching nearest station to Matheran (Neral) : 8:30 Am Reaching hill station : by 10 Am maximum and exploring it till 7 PM and returning hostel by 10 PM maximum. And that's how everything happened… Right? Answer over, no go and read some other post… Hell no! It is monsoon and it rains whole fkin day in Mumbai (atleast whenever I plan something), even when I was making up this plan it was raining in the college. I slept at 2:15 Am, I started watching memes with the friends and slept late. I usually keep my phone in silent mode, and when I was setting up the alarm, I turned the volume of everything to full except Alarm. Alarm volume was 0. I woke up at 8 Am🙂 I was thinking what to do as I had only one class, that too of a humanities elective and it was first lecture so, it was completely skippable. I was deciding what to do, so I decided to get out of comfort zone, pack the bag and leave for the place. Earlier, I was planning to leave empty stomach and eat at the hill station but now, I can have my meal in mess… I ate enough in the mess and saved banana for the trip. (Mess gives 1 banana everyday.) I was ready by 9:15 AM. What I packed in the bag : 1 Pen, 1 Notebook, “The Psychology of Money” book, a small towel, Face Wash, Mobile Charger, Water bottle, Wallet (₹700 Cash in it) and all the cards. Since it was raining, I decided to book ride online. For me, Indian ride hailing apps always sucks, and Uber provide me driver in the first go. I got uber driver with average rating of 4.94 star rated by some 800+ people, I was amazed of his rating and he was good, I rated him 5 star too. The ride costed me ₹114, it is a lot but worth it as it was raining that time. I reached Kanjurmarg station (railway station nearest to my college) by 9:40 Am. I didn't bought ticket as the queue was long. I got confused on the central line, like the thing is that complicated that I can't explain to non-mumbaikers. (For mumbaikers only, I had to take local to Neral station… as I stepped on the first train, It was slower train till Badlapur and I don't know what tf was going in my mind, I get off of it at Thane. At Thane (I waited for 10 mins) and then I boarded faster local (which was till Badlapur)… as my train arrived on Dombivali, I got confused that I come far already and I come out of train… but soon I realised that Kalyaan comes after Dombivali… I waited 10 min at Dombivali and boarded faster local for Titwala, so I boarded the train and come out at Kalyan. At Kalyan, I waited for 25–30 min and then slow local for Badlapur arrives. At Badlapur, I got another local(till Karjat) in 2 minutes.) In short, I wasted almost 1 hr on different stations. and I reached Neral station at around 12 PM. As I came out of station, I saw a Hitachi ATM and I got happy as I needed some ₹100–200 notes but one person in the ATM was doing something else in it, I don't know, he had connected his laptop and was coding something and he didn't let me enter the ATM. Anyways, I asked Auto Driver to drop me at Matheran and he said (he said in hindi but for Quora policy, I'm writing in English), “You are alone?” “Yes” “Then, do cab… renting Auto will be expensive. Cab will charge ₹100” “Sure, Thanks” I got cab instantly as the driver needed just 1 passenger to fill his car completely. I reached Matheran by 12:20. Cab costed me ₹100. My total expenditure = ₹214. Then, I bought the ticket (₹50), a plastic raincoat (₹100), a mobile rain protector and a cap (₹60 combined) Total expenditure till now = ₹424 Then, I did one wrong thing… instead of entering from the entrance, I started entering from the exit… Poor me, I walked 1Km just to realise that I'm going the wrong way. Then, I entered the correct way and it was around 12:40 PM. Again, I got confused and started roaming mindlessly, like I was seeing random things (those random things were rare for me.) Then, I remembered that I saw on a YouTube video that you need to take e-rickshaw or Horse to reach Matheran hill station. I saw an auto driver and instantly got my co-passengers… He dropped me at Matheran hill top by 1:20 PM almost. Total expenditure = ₹424 + 35 = ₹459. It started raining, and I used raincoat and mobile cover… I was ready for the exploration. I went to first point… I don't know the name but I saw nothing from there… I went to 3 more points but didn't got any significant view. I got hungry and bought some snacks worth ₹48 (MRP ₹40), two packet lays, 1 packet of bourbon biscuit and 1 packet of Oreo. Total expenditure = ₹507 I ate a packet of Lays and saw an outlet selling something… I ate Maggi there along with a bottle of Pepsi. Who tf eat Maggi with Pepsi… Me! Both costed me total ₹110. My total expenditure = ₹617. I started looking for some ATM and saw an ATM by Vakrangee (last year, I did my biggest profit in this company, it was 150% ig) and I withdraw ₹500 from there. As I came out of restaurant, I started walking for better view of the valley… (Some garden ig) and a puppy started following me… he/she (whoever it was)… he saw so cute, like I couldn't resist giving him my packet of biscuit. But… As I opened the packet and kept infront of him, 5–6 monkeys came there and they didn't let him eat those. I think that puppy only got 1. Those bully monkeys took away 5–6 biscuits. Anyways, I didn't clicked those monkeys as I wanted to keep my phone safe, there might be possibility that they take my phone from me. Yes! monkey did this with one guy (as told by restaurant owner) Anyways, I went ahead and 3 dogs started looking at me… I gave them another pack of biscuit (my last) As I torn the pack and threw at them, the main dog (the dog which was closet to packet) didn't know how to tore it completely… other 2 dogs didn't cared much and let him handle it alone. And when the 2 dogs went far, the main dog tear the packet and ate entire stuff alone. I was like… damn! dude got brain… I started walking and suddenly I realised I'm alone. Alone on a road like this… I threw my bag on the side… turned off earphones…. Played my favourite travel song (The Nights) and did signature move of Ronaldo… and I randomly started running, no matter if it was downslope or upslope… even when I saw some people, I was just running with arms open.. (Let me tell you it was raining entire time at the place) It was wet floor and I was running as fast as I can, singing my favourite music as loud as I can no matter if 5 people are watching me or some 10 people are observing. I ran a lot, I sang a lot. untill the path got narrower and suddenly I realised I'm lost. I saw one couple (young), I got calm else I was taking some stress at that moment) Suddenly I saw some fog… I went ahead saw 4 people smoking cigarettes. They offered me, I denied. They asked me my hat to shot photos and when I handed it to them, they offered it to monkey. Fortunately, monkeys didn't reacted much. I didn't wanted to waste my time on those creeps, I decided to walk ahead. Boom! I reached Charlotte Lake. Like can you imagine… 10 min ago, I was like I am lost and now, there are atleast 100 people around me, 100 is wrong, atleast 250 people around me. I spent some time there. I wanted to take bath like the ones jnthe picture but I didn't bought clothes with me otherwise an introvert guy could be seen taking bath there. That's exactly why I went for solo trip… I can be myself, no matter how close the friend is, we can't be 100% of who we are with someone. I was just being myself today. Anyways, I just washed my hands and moved away. I saw downslope way… I did my favourite thing, running with arms open while singing my favourite travel song (it was being played simultaneously on my mobile too).. I couldn't do that infront of my friends. Like I was enjoying something after a long time. It was first day I didn't got the thought of opening social media, I was just using camera app..I didn't used YouTube, I just dialled my mum’s number… Like I was doing something that my brain actually wants. I reached another point ( I don't remember the name), Its name was something like Edward point and I saw something like this… And with this view, my mission got completed. (It was raining whole time btw.) Haan, before reaching the above point, something happened with me. 6–7 people were drinking alcohol and they were drunk AF. They offered me one bottle for ₹90 along with some snacks. Obviously, I rejected. 2 women observed this and they thought that those guys are bullying me, the two women started favouring me and started verbally abusing the 6–7 people. Like… even I'm confused what the hell happened there. At the above point, I bought a Sting bottle as I was running out of energy. The bottle of sting costed me ₹30. Total Expenditure = ₹647. I randomly started walking freely and saw 2 guys clicking their photo. I asked them to click my photo and they did the same. The two guys had a speaker but they didn't have songs and I have songs but not a big speaker… I joined them and now, we went to 3–4 points clicked some photos but randomly heavy rain came and I got wet, all of my bag, clothes, book, notebook got wet. Actually, I took off my raincoat just half an hr. ago. We went 3–4 more points but nothing special visible from there.. Anyways, then, I walked back, sometimes running the same way! Spent ₹160 more to reach my hostel. Total Expenditure = ₹807 Solo trips are too good, you do things that you can't even imagine you can do. I came out of my comfort zone, but fog disturbed my experience a bit. Anyways, that's it for now. ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Question: Were you ever a victim of fraud or a scam? If so, what happened?
Answer: Yes, just two days ago on 28 Jul, 2024. I was leaving for Mumbai for my third year and I was boarding my train from New Delhi railway station (NDLS). I took a metro to New Delhi metro station and travelled to railway station. My train was scheduled to arrive on Platform 1 at 4:55 PM and I don't know why I reached there at 4:10 PM. I was exhausted as it was 44-45°C and I sweated so much that my entire t-shirt was wet and my brain was not working due to all this. (Remember that the train was scheduled on Platform 1.) And that's how problem started, literally every word in the above paragraph was the reason I got scammed. I reached the platform 1 on 4:10 PM and as I completed walking down the stairs, a person come to me and said (he said in hindi but I'm writing in English for Quora policy), “Can you please let me use your phone?” “Why?” “Actually, someone has stolen my mobile phone and wallet and I need to check the platform in which my train will arrive” “Okay, let me know your train, I'll see on the app and will tell you.” (He said that his train is Paschim Express) I opened the app and typed Paschim Express, there were two options for that train, one was regular and one was special train. He checked the timing of the one that comes above (special) and it was expected to leave New Delhi on 4:45 PM. Then he said that his ticket is not confirmed and asked me if I can I give him some money. He said that he is travelling to Mumbai and will give me my money through UPI ( remember the term UPI) on reaching his home. I asked him how much, he said ₹1500. (Remember the 1500 figure) I mostly use my mobile to do payments and I do not use cash. I just had only ₹500 that time and I told him exactly the same. He said that we can visit some shop, scan the QR and get money there. We travelled to platform 7, I don't know why he took me to platform 7 but I will tell later how platform 7 is important in this story. We asked some shops but they denied giving us cash. I suggested that we can visit ATM outside and can get cash from there. On our way to ATM (which was approx 500m from P-7) he asked basic things about me and said that he has iPhone 14 Pro Max and he is worried as his account has ₹4–5lac. Not gonna lie, I got some little sense of what's happening at this point cuz I never asked him about his mobile and bank balance. On our way to ATM, he said, “I'm glad that we met otherwise I couldn't get a chance to reach home, my mother has some disease and it's important for me to reach home” Further he said, “It is not about money, it is about the time… money come and go” And he further added, “Thank You for helping me, kind people like you are very rare.” I don't why my emotional side dominated at that place and I imagined myself at his place and I believed that he is genuine. On the way, he took my phone number and noted on a piece of paper.. he asked my number, so my trust increased. Till we reached the ATM, he repeated the same words again and again to not my brain think and he kept me busy so that I didn't get a chance to think about him. He said me that Kind people like you are very rare. The guy looked like 24–26 Y/O, he was bright colored (skin tone similar to SRK, like I'm taking only about skin tone)… he was carrying one red colored bag, dressed well… like dressed better than me, so I thought he is genuine. Like he was never silent, always talking and my brain was busy in processing his words. When we reached the ATM, I asked him how much he wants, he said ₹2500. Due to all the heat waves outside, my wet t-shirt and everything, my brain didn't thought that earlier he asked for ₹1500. I don't why, I agreed. There were three ATMs of 3 PSU banks. 2 of them were not functioning, one of Indian Bank was functioning which has 2 machines inside it, since outside was a queue, the security guard didn't let him inside, idk maybe he was coming to see my ATM PIN. The machine was only processing notes of ₹200 and asking me to type in multiple in ₹200, I thought for a while and arrived at withdrawing ₹2800. When I come out of ATM, he immediately come towards me (not in a suspicious way) like everything was good good… he asked me about how much I withdraw, I gave him ₹2600. Why? I don't know… while writing this, it looks like I scammed myself. Since it was 4:30 PM already, and my train was scheduled to arrive nearly the same time, I'm a safe player, we headed towards station. On the way to platform 5 (Stations were lined up from 16 to 1, so they were in decreasing order of number) On the escalator, I asked his and his family members’ phone number, he gave me 2 number, one of his mom and one of him only. Fool me! I didn't dialled his mom's number at that moment. Only thing I did in the entire event was believing him, and I think that's exactly where I fucked up. Another mistake, since my train was 10 min later than his, I didn't went with him to make sure he boarded the train. Last I saw him was when he was walking down the escalator. Everything ended. At around 1–2 PM, IRCTC messaged me and told that my train will arrive on P-1 and that's why I stepped there. Plot twist : My train arrived on platform 3. It was around 4:40 PM that I realised my train will come on P-3 (I checked using ixigo as train generally arrive 30–40 min before leaving.) I took my seat around 4:45 PM, my mum called him to ask me I have took my seat and like 2–3 people confirmed by calling me. It was around 5:10, I don't know how I got the thought of calling his mom's number. And guess what… Number doesn't exist. And I dialled his number… now guess what… Number exist but it was not available for incoming calls. I checked if UPI is registered for the number.. And guess what… UPI was registered but its name was different on GPay. He told me he is Deepak from Andheri… but everything was a lie. By 5:15 PM, i realised that I was scammed with ₹2600. Only thing I was happied was about the one ₹200 note that I didn't gave him. What's my fault? Believing someone who said that he is in problem? He said that people like me are very kind and very rare. Bro, now such people will be even more rarer, atleast the number of such people is X-1 (if it was X earlier) And atleast, how can you scam someone who was trying to help you…. Whatever…. I will title this as I scammed myself. If IRCTC informed me correctly, I would've never stepped on P-1 and thus, it wouldn't happened. I went to college and only thing hopping in my mind, not mind but entire body was this incident. Want more of this story? You'll be like I'm make up things now… In my college, I discussed this story with my friend… he was scammed the same way with ₹1000 on IGI Airport on 25 July in a similar way. The person could be different… maybe same , the story was different, the amount was different. For sure, the number of people who can help a random people are decreased by atleast 2. I was disappointed not because of money but because of cheating, because of misuse of trust. That's it. Delhi is not for beginners, wait… I'm living in Ghaziabad for 18 years (Ghaziabad is worse than Delhi)… Delhi or even whole NCR is not even for experts. ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Question: Is NIRF ranking worth true and considering?
Answer: I have exactly different opinion on NIRF rankings from other people who have answered this. Inshort, Yes! they are true and worth considering. First, let's understand the criteria of NIRF rankings… Except the Graduation Outcomes, which holds just 20% of weightage, most of the colleges in India are no different. Whether it is IIT or VIT, Indian mindset is not research oriented as we don't see direct benefit in it. 90% of IIT teachers don't give a fuck to students, so first point is also not a differentiator. Perception, now see.. government (NIRF) can't say that NIT is good and SRM is all bad, I know it is bad but you can't say to them straightforward, atleast govt. can't say to 10K students that you are in a bad institute. Simple! Most people say that IIIT Delhi ranks less than Amity. It's just unfair… According to me, it's not unfair. Just assume for a second, that students in VIT, SRM, Amity and all these colleges are offered similar paychecks as the ones from IITs. Will you still say that ranking Amity above IIITD is unfair? No, right. As we are judging solely on the basis of placements and that's exactly how we should not look at NIRF rankings. We are not judging colleges, I mean, atleast normal people are just judging colleges based on news headlines which is not fine in my opinion. In my opinion, the purpose of a university should be that it should make a person employable not employed. After his graduation, he should be left on his own to find work. And when it comes to making their students employable, IIT and VIT are no different, their curriculum is mostly same like more than 90%, their labs are similar (trust me, IIT labs are fucked up, lab equipments don't work a lot of times). The only difference is the students, we can't deny that students in IIT and pvt. colleges are different in terms of IQ, seriousness in life, and all. (See clearly that I never said who is better or worse, I just mentioned that they are different.) But wait… NIRF judges college? not students? Right? I don't know how to end this post but… hope you got my point that the way we look at colleges is not good. Plus, 90% of companies that visit IITs also visits VIT and all the top private colleges for that matter. (Only consulting companies, HFTs and some rare firms don't visit private colleges) To conclude, when we judge colleges, we judge students and when NIRF judges, it judges everything. Question: What are the 10 things you regret doing in your life?
Answer: Honestly, I don't have much regrets. Only regret I have in my life is giving up on my YouTube dream. I got exposed to YouTube when I was in class 6 and my father bought a second hand mobile phone, and not gonna lie, from the very beginning, I was more enthusiastic about the upload feature in the app more than the view one. I created many channels, more than 10 in numbers in different timeline but I would mention stories of the two channels where I spent more than 80% of my time. My most successful channel was created when I was in class 8. I had around 75–80 videos that got about 18K cumulative views which earned me around 800 subscribers. However, one random day, YouTube deleted my channel due to strikes from music labels and game developers. I used to create videos related to games not exactly like gameplay but telling people about games like its history, giving them safe mods, and all. This was one and only smartphone in the house, and it got some problems when I was in class 9, which shattered everything. We were living with a keypad phone for next 2 years. My cousin (whom I used hate then and even now) used to have an extra phone which was of Intex brand, she used to keep it idle like it was of no use to her, but since I hated her, I never asked her to give it to me, infact she used to hate me too (some family issues). So, whenever she used to go out, I use that phone to create videos and before she come, I just put it at that same place so that she doesn't know. I used to save my money to do recharge for internet. One day I missed putting the phone at the right place and she saw me, I just asked her to give it to me and she declined that she needed that one too, but she was just making excuses. Anyways, another time my dream was broken and I never touched that phone again. Then, after my class 10 board exams, which ended on 18 March 2020, we bought a new phone. The first thing I did with that phone was creating a new YouTube channel, even though I had no clear idea of what content to make. I started creating same game related videos, the content that I wished existed. During those days, I was crazy for YouTube, even much more than IIT during my JEE prep. If someone had told me back then that I would clear JEE Advanced two years later, I wouldn't have believed them. In fact, I would laughed at them. It was only smartphone in our family which my father used to take with him to work. He would leave at 9:30 AM and come back at 9 PM. I used to wake up at 4 AM and go to the terrace of my house to record voiceovers while hiding from the neighbors, otherwise they would think I'm psycho. My mom used to wake up at 6 AM to bring milk, so to get extra time, I started bringing milk instead of her so that she don't notice me and I would wake her up at 7 AM, and then leave for school. So, all in all, I had only 3 (or 3.5 max.) hours to do the job. Honestly, I was so dedicated to YouTube that I would automatically wake up at 4 AM without any alarm. We were a joint family back then, and my grandparents used to wake up at 4 AM, so it was like ki if I'm waking at 4 AM, it's Ok but not if I wake up before that my parents would ask me to sleep. There were many instances where I woke up at 2 AM and went to the washroom to check my channel stats because of that 4 AM thing, and I used to spent 2 hrs. there in hot April weather without any fan or anything and I used to see all the stats. I can't tell how much involved I was. Again, problem started. One neighbour saw me for several days and complained to my mom that he (me) talks to someone everyday for 3 hrs, I used to record voice for my videos so she thought like this. My mum ignored, I mean she didn't ignored but didn't reacted. A lot of neighbours started complaining the same, she thought I'm ruining her image in the neighbourhood, but still she didn't reacted. She listened me talking something but didn't reacted as I used create videos in English which was improving my vocabulary and english speaking too. My channel grew to some 400 subscribers in just 1 month and around 8–10k views in 30 videos before something happened. One random day, me and my brother started fighting for mobile(which is common between siblings) and he complained to my mom about my channel. I won't say she scolded me, she sort of tortured me and beat me a lot, like a lot like the same way police will treat a terrorist. I don't want to remember what happened that day, surely it was one of the worst day of my life. A creator was literally killed that day. My brother deleted everything, my channel, all of my screenshots, my editing apps, my voiceovers, everything. Finally, my YouTube fever got over, and some days later, I randomly started my JEE prep, did well and got into a decent college. The neighbour to tell her first and spreaded all this in the neighbourhood was jealous of me as her son and daughter were my classmates and I was far ahead of them, I got 93% in class 12th where her son scored 72% and daughter scored 71% and I took revenge with her face being pale that day. My channel got deleted in May 2020 and result came on 15 July. In class 12, her son scored less than 60% and daughter scored around 75% despite both of them being studious and taking tuitions worth 1000s a month and I did everything from YouTube. I don't know but… Hsssh, let's stop for now. Question: How does the stock market work? Who decides the price of stocks? What is the logic behind the valuation of stocks?
Answer: Ok. I'll keep this it as simple as possible. How does the stock market work? The stock market is where investors (either people or firms) buy and sell shares of public companies. When you buy a stock, you own a small piece of that company. It is similar to olx (where people trade used goods) and in stock market (after making profit or loss) people trade ownership of companies. Who decides the price of stocks? The price of a stock is determined by the supply and demand for that stock. When more people want to buy a stock (demand) than sell it (supply), the stock price goes up. When more people want to sell than buy, the price goes down. In short, it is determined by people participating in it. Consider Meat to be a stock, If more people want meat (let's say during Ramadan), obviously, the price will go up as retailer will try to earn as much as possible and will make more money. If people want less meat (let's say during Saawan), the retailer will short of customer and will try to sell at lower price (as meat will rot after some time), so the price will go down. See, on any given day, the no. of times a particular stock is sold is same as the no. of times a particular stock is purchased. (Agar kisine meat bechi, tabhi to koi kharidega na, sellers need buyers, right?) (Obviously, no. of buyers = no. of sellers but the main word is demand.) What is the logic behind the valuation of stocks? The valuation of a stock depends on many factors, including the company's financial performance, growth potential, industry trends, and overall economic conditions. Investors analyze these factors to estimate the intrinsic value of a stock and decide whether it is undervalued or overvalued. For example, if a company consistently generates strong profits and has a promising future outlook, investors may be willing to pay a higher price for its stock. On the other hand, if a company is struggling financially or faces significant challenges, its stock price may be lower. (Obviously, Paneer is sold for higher price than potato because it is more valuable, has more nutrients. The same case is with companies.) A particular ownership of Reliance is worth more than that of LIC because It has more value, Reliance make more money per 0.01% of company than LIC, hence its stock is priced more. Question: What made you smile today?
Answer: Ok. On June 19, My laptop started having some problems with charging and turning on. I took it to a service center and got it repaired in two days. At the service center, I got to know that my laptop adapter had also stopped working. The problem was actually with the adapter, which caused issues with the motherboard of the laptop. [Technical details : Asus Vivobook laptop adapters come in two power variations, 45W and 65W. The 45W adapter comes in 4mm, 4.5mm, and 5.5mm diameter pins, while the 65W adapter has convertible pin option. Over time, they are switching to smaller options to make their laptops slimmer, and now they only launch laptops with 4mm pins. Problem start with the fact that diameter of my laptop charging pin is 4.5mm.] (This is my laptop btw, does everything I want like I don't play games, I don't use heavy stuff, It just works fine and gives around 5hr. of battery life even after 2 years of extensive usage.) Coming back to the story, I asked him for the adaptor too. The store manager asked me to wait for 30 minutes while they contacted other store to get the adapter (all the exclusive stores of a particular brand are connected). I waited, and the guy came back with a 4mm adapter. They asked me to come back the next day, and I agreed, thinking at least my laptop was repaired. There's a place in my city where all the electronics brands have their stores, and there are many multi-brand stores too. I think every city has a similar place. Anyway, I visited all the stores but couldn't find an adapter with the desired specifications. I visited 10–12 other stores in the nearby area but couldn't find the desired product. I went back on June 22, but they still didn't have the adapter, so I had to return empty-handed. This time, the store manager asked me to call them before coming. I looked online but couldn't find an original adapter that met the specifications. I called them on June 24, and some other guy picked up who couldn't understand the difference between 4mm and 4.5mm and misinformed me that they had the adapter. I went to the store but found nothing. I tried another store, but it wasn't there either. I called them again on June 25, and they said their stock would arrive in two days. I agreed. I called again on June 27, and they gave the same reply. At this point, I called 15-20 Asus exclusive stores (got their numbers via Google Maps), but none of them had the adapter I needed. I lost hope, thinking I would have to buy a new laptop, but I didn't want to do that as I had a lot of data and photos in it. I called again on june 28 and 29, but they still gave the same response that stock would arrive in 1-2 days. My brother suggested me to go to Nehru Place and try to find it there. Today (30 June), I Googled and found an exclusive store there. Nehru Place was 35 km from my place, so I took the metro, spent 2 hours, and reached there. The store manager told me: "This specification adapter won't be available. Did you buy it online?" "Yes." "It might be imported from China, so finding the adapter is impossible." I left the store with no hope of finding the adapter. I was just deciding whether to take risk and get 65W variant or exchange this laptop for a newer one and decided to go back to the metro station. On my way back to the metro station, I saw another store. I had zero hope, no expectations, no faith, nothing. I just stepped in the store like some skeleton and asked the guy there, "Do you have a 45W adapter with a 4.5mm pin?" "Yes." A miracle. I can't tell how happy I was when I saw what I wanted, a small laptop charger. I got the original adapter for a price 15% lower than what the Ghaziabad store was charging (that too from an exclusive store, so 0 probability of fake product). The attempt in which I had zero hope got me the product at a very good price. And the attempts in which I was 100% sure gave me nothing more than disappointment. This is just another day of me realizing that life gives you the most when you expect the least. Me and my IIT friends have experienced and observed this thing and discussed multiple times that life become atleast 10X better when you stop expecting things, I can't tell you how much this hack has improved my life, like I can't tell. Ngl, this made me smile really well. Sometimes, we take important things for granted. Learning for you : Buy a laptop that supports Type-C charging. (Btw, how is the skin of my laptop?) That's it. ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Question: Can you share something random with me?
Answer: Birthday Paradox, a quite interesting topic. (It is also called the birthday problem where you have to find the probability of atleast 2 people having same birthday) Okay. Let's begin. The birthday paradox is counterintuitive fact that in a group of just 23 people, there is a 50% probability that at least two people will share the same birthday. Here's a concise explanation: The birthday paradox arises because the probability of at least two people sharing a birthday increases much more rapidly than one might expect as the group size grows. This is due to the exponential nature of the probability calculations. Okay, let's do calculations. Continue from here only if you want to dive deep into mathematics and knows basic class 12 probability. Probability of Unique Birthdays Suppose there are n people in a group. The probability that the first person has a unique birthday is 1. The probability that the second person has a unique birthday is 364/365, since there are 364 days left in the year that are not the same as the first person's birthday. The probability that the third person has a unique birthday is 363/365, and so on. The probability that all n people have unique birthdays is: P(all unique birthdays) = 1 × 364/365 × 363/365 × ... × (365-n+1)/365 Probability of at Least Two Shared Birthdays The probability of at least two people sharing a birthday is the complement of the probability that all birthdays are unique: P(at least two shared birthdays) = 1 - P(all unique birthdays) Substituting the expression from above: P(at least two shared birthdays) = 1 - (1 × 364/365 × 363/365 × ... × (365-n+1)/365) Calculating the Probability for 23 People Now, let's plug in n = 23 people: P(at least two shared birthdays) = 1 - (1 × 364/365 × 363/365 × ... × 343/365) P(at least two shared birthdays) ≈ 0.5073 or 50.73% So, with a group of 23 people, the probability of at least two people sharing a birthday is approximately 50.73%, or just over 50%. Hope you got it. Ask if you have any doubt. That's it for now. ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Question: What is a share?
Answer: Ok. Imagine you run a milk distribution business named Pan Parag Milkies, basically that dudhwala, you take milk at ₹40 per litre from the farmers and sell it to consumers for ₹70 a litre, and let me suppose you sell the milk to 100 consumers and all of them take 1L per day. Your profit per month = ( (70–40) × 30 × 100 ) = ₹90K per month (excluding the wastage, logistics and bad transactions) Your life is going all fine, but now your kids grown up, their demands went up, their girlfriends are asking for gifts from them, they want their man to pay in restaurants, they want to go to abroad to study, they want PS5, they want iPhones to show off, they want to go to Dubai and do everything which is not possible from current income. So, You decide to scale your business to earn more, you want to set up a milk processing plant that cost ₹1 Cr. with which you decide to package the milk and sell it to more and more consumers, even in foreign. But you don't have the money and no one is giving you money on loan. You decide to list your company on stock market and raise money from common people, Imagine you decided to raise ₹1.5 Cr and sell off your 40% ownership in the company. You decided to split your company in 1 Lac pieces and decided to sell off 40% of them at ₹375 per share (to raise ₹1.5 Cr.) in short, you sold 40% of your business, you can't do anything on your own, you have to listen to your shareholders for every major move. Now, the process through which you list your company on stock market is called IPO, initial public offering. You can raise only certain amount depending on the profits of your company. This minimum ownership of your company will be called a share, in this case, it is 1/100k which is 0.001% ownership per share. Many people confuse between share and stock, simple, stock is Pan Parag Milkies and share is what you buy and sell, i.e, what you trade, i.e. what you purchased for ₹375. Hope you got everything. ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Question: How stock market operators manipulate stocks?
Answer: This is going to be interesting, stay till the very end. Ever heard of the company PC Jewellers? Yes, that same damn company which disturbed our TV during childhood, It's stock was manipulated by famous stock operator Ketan Parikh. Let's start with an example. Imagine you purchased a wheat bag for ₹1000 and now you want to multiply your money with it. But how it is possible? You can hardly sell this bag for a maximum of ₹1100 or 1200? That too after 1 or 2 year? So how to make more money? By creating more demand. You decide to invest / spend ₹500 and gave a piece of it to many potential buyers, media companies, brokers, retailers and spreaded news that your wheat bag is better than others… Now you go to market everyday for bidding on your bag, and those paid buyers increased the price of your wheat bag by bidding more than what it should, seeing the demand of the price, it attracted actual wheat buyers, then they saw on news channel that your wheat bag is better. And guess what…. You ended up selling the same damn bag for ₹10,000. Yes, a huge 9X return - 0.5X investment = 8.5X final return. The difference between my assumption and actual manipulation is the amount of money involved, instead of ₹500, they use ₹10–50 Cr. to increase share price to 100X even. This is more or less how operators manipulate the stock, and the same happened with PCJ stock when Ketan Parikh, the guy banned from Indian Stock Market, manipulated the stock while living in UK, just only using his connections with brokers, media houses, banks, and other institutions. And then, when the stock price is higher, they sell off their stock, which leads to decrease in the stock price and coming it to same people. At the end, operators made money, retail investors lost. This thing is called Pump and Dump. Let's look at PCJ stock He took some time and did the stuff slowly but whatever it is, it is clear and there are evidences that PCJ was manipulated by operators. Ketan Parikh was barred from stock trading on Dec 2003 for 14 years due to similar kind of work, but he didn't stopped and no one knows if he is doing similar stuff now. I observed one stock named Praveg went from ₹3 to ₹1200 in just 3 years, which might be manipulated. That stock is dying now, and is at ₹800. That's it. ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Question: What is something people need to realise?
Answer: Everything is temporary. Failed your exam? Missing your childhood days? Your crush rejected you? Don't have much friends? Struggling with current job? Classmates bullying? I was unhappy with my semester 3 grades, but somehow I realised I can't do anything with it and stopped thinking about it, and now I'm happy with whatever I got. Eventually, dots will connect automatically better than how you were trying to, you just need to think about the dots 24*7. Once you stop thinking about them, then there might be some problems, but again, take it easy. So, don't take much stress, I believe that life is Health : 25% Job/Money : 10% hardly Relationships : 15% max. Being happy : 50%+ So, take it easy and enjoy, throw this mobile and go out (abhi nahi, abhi bahar 43°C hai) and do things you are wishing to do 5–10 years later, you don't never know if you live till then. 10 years down the line, you'll laugh on the things about which you are depressed right now. You might miss these nights in which you are stressed about something. That's it. If you've reached here, ho sake toh for the next 30 min. after this post, do the thing what you like the most, whether it is cricket, gossiping, cooking, talking with the special person, startgazing or whatever. and repeat this daily! ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Question: What is the craziest story you heard in IIT Bombay?
Answer: This story is of my friend, Pinku. Pinku was a fresher at IIT Bombay in 2022. He was an introvert, though he did have some friends, sort of a fractional introvert. It was Pinku's first chemistry lab when it happened - he got a crush on a girl, Jivika at first sight. Luckily, Pinku's hostel was H16, which was co-ed, separated by buildings but better than other hostels. From his room, he could see his crush going to classes, walking around campus. He could see her in the mess. Though Pinku was often late for regular classes, he always made sure to arrive 10 minutes early for labs, so he could partner with his crush. Interestingly, she never rejected the idea of being his lab partner. And Pinku acted very normal around her, not letting on about his feelings. They became close friends, exchanged phone numbers, and used to chat on Instagram and WhatsApp. Except for Instagram chats, it was always her who used to start the conversation. Whenever she saw him in the mess and the general shop, she used to give him a sweet smile that always melted his heart. The same semester, they had another lab course, MakerSpace (MS101), which combined mechanical, computer science, and electrical concepts. It gave insight into real engineering, with students having to make a line following bot as the project. They got labs in the course too, and used to talk a lot. Pinku used to make her laugh a lot. They used to talk a lot. It was everytime Jivika who used to start the conversation while walking on the road. But Pinku didn't confess anything. The second semester came with a Physics lab. They used to talk a lot, and Pinku used to talk to her and vice versa. Both used to talk the most. Slowly, half of the class started knowing that Pinku liked Jivika. Most probably, someone had told her about Pinku, but her nature remained the same. She always used to react to Pinku's Instagram stories. He always used to post close friends stories, in which only Jivika was a close friend. She used to react to more than half of Pinku's Instagram stories. The second semester ended, still Pinku didn't confess anything. Pinku changed his branch, and slowly their 1-hour Instagram chats decreased to 30 minutes by the end of the 2nd semester. They reduced to 10 minutes by the start of the 3rd semester. By the start of the 3rd semester, they only started asking one question. As stated, Pinku was an introvert. He didn't get any reason to talk to her. He always felt that she would not like him. It's the end of the 4th semester. Pinku hasn't talked to her for the past 6 months, neither online nor face-to-face. Maybe she knows everything but didn't react. Maybe Pinku was too introverted. Whatever the case, both are single now, working on their careers. When asked what if she's happy with someone else, Pinku replied, "I'm happy if she's happy, all I want is her being happy and enjoying her life." That's it. The story is real, Pinku and Jivika are dummy names to maintain their privacy. ~ Trying to live a life worth remembering

Question: What's your take on reservations? When will it end?
Answer: I'm gonna get a lot of hate with this answer, but ya, i'mma definitely writing this one. For next 5 minutes, just think rationally, forget the college seat, forget the job, forget everything, then proceed further. And don't make any opinion without completing reading the entire post. Before starting, let me introduce myself, I come under OBC-NCL category, my JEE Advanced rank was 5K, enough to fetch me any IIT irrespective of category. And, OBC-NCL reservation is sort of EWS which is more of income basis than caste. For my seat, the rankings of different male students were: Gen - 2.1K Gen EWS - 4K OBC NCL - 5.6K SC - 16K ST - 35K+ PWD - A guy with 500K mains rank ((has no adv rank) is studying) To those who don't know: The criteria for EWS & OBC student is family income less than 8LPA. Let's see take on reservation of India's top ranked (acc. to QS rankings) university : (Random photo I took 2 years back during my IITB orientation) In my opinion, Reservation is the product of caste system. Untill caste system disappear, It is not possible to abolish reservations. Ok, it's not possible to remove it next minute. It's much complicated that you, me and anybody know. First of all, no government will want to remove it, There is a huge votebank in India for the parties that supports some particular castes, in my area, SP and BSP are ex. of such parties. And as I have said in the past too, top leaders don't care about anything other than power. You might know the BR Ambedkar story, which motivated him to introduce the system. Well, the thing is real, some community people are abused with the words like c****r. And getting to more deeper, there are many tribal areas in India, where people are unaware of internet, I think it's not unfair they can't compete with general students ever. I saw a video by YouTuber Sarthak Goswami, [will find the put the video in comments, must watch that] where he went to a village where there was a one room school with no teacher nothing, that too upto class 5. Watching that video, I realised how privileged are the people who are reading this, we have not seen the world, we have just saw big schools, coaching centres, YouTube videos, games like PUBG, FF, Big Boss, Elvish Yadav, Barbie vs Oppenheimer, Starbucks, and we assume that we know everything, I realised hardly we know 10% of the stuff. When will it abolish? I don't think in next 3 decades atleast, unless people starts living together and stop every sort of caste related discrimination, honesty, It doesn't make sense to remove it. Caste system is a bigger problem than reservation for the society. Remember hate against each other divided India in 1947, not the seats. Hate is bigger curse. Temporary / Immediate solution There is a girl in my class who earlier had 70K OP 11 Pro, and now had iPhone 14 Pro, I don't know her category but her rank was 50k+ in mains and no rank in advanced (that means above 35k). I think such people don't deserve reservation who are good at everything except caste. Just like there is income cap for General and OBC students, there should be income cap for SC and ST students. But I feel that 8 LPA is much higher cap, It should be reduced to 3 LPA maximum for all the categories same. Another problem I have met a lot of EWS students (Gen EWS) and all of them categorically said that their EWS certificate is fake and when I asked why? They said everyone else's too is fake. And believe me, 90% of income certificates are fake in my college. The reason for this is corruption, you pay someone ₹2k, you'll get EWS certificate next day. At the end, things are not that straightforward, it will take time but we are moving in the right direction. That's it. Question: Do most stock traders really earn money?
Answer: No, It is not possible for traders to earn money unless they have some insider news or they are selling course. First let's understand a game theory called Zero Sum game, which no one tells, literally no one and I think this theory can change the way people look at wealth. Zero Sum Game Imagine two people (Ramu and Shamu) are betting ₹10-₹10 each on India and Sri Lanka match, Ramu will win if India wins, Shamu wins other case. Now, Imagine if India wins. Hence, Ramu won ₹10 and Shamu lost the same amount. Now, add the profit of all the parties involved = 10 (Ramu) + (-10(Shamu) = 0 This is called Zero Sum game, when sum of profits of all parties is zero. People can never make money for long term in this case. Now, Imagine you invited your friend to manage the bet (say Kitu). You both pays ₹1 to him and 19 will be distributed among you. Now, add profits of all the persons involved, It will be -₹1. Now, there are two things: 1. Investing Investing is like you put your savings and let it grow, you don't do much activity here, Investing adds value to the society you literally owns some part of a business. 2. Trading It is a Zero Sum game. No value addition, no long term income. In trading if you are earning something, then someone is losing his money. One day, you'll lose your money and someone else earn. Meanwhile government will earn brokerage, taxes and transaction charges (It's good for them). Just a meme :) Signing Off Vansh Yadav

Question: What is an incident that changed your life?
Answer: False police case against my father and brother. This story is of about 2013, when I was in Class 4 that time, a very average guy, my brother was in class 7, he too an average guy in academics but good at sports. There was a family in the area that has 4 members, a man, a woman, their son and their daughter. They used to sell affordable alcohol bottles and drugs. Although those days, their this business was in the starting phase. It was all illegal but who cares, in that era, police, rules and regulations were not that prevalent. (Image picked from Google) One day, me and my brother (let's call him H) and some 8–10 boys from the same area were playing in the ground. It was a normal cricket match with red leather ball. H was fielding at the time (I was also fielding, but my brother is the main character) The location is about 100m from my home. Someone hit the ball and It goes near the guy marked as J (he is the son of drug seller). At that time, no one knows they used to sell drugs, they were common people back then. Ok, as the ball was near J and my brother was fielding, he went to pick it up, and J started abusing him for no reason. My brother ignored him and threw the ball near the playing area. He started abusing again. The convo turned into a small fight, my brother went near him and somehow his arm got injured. He started crying, all the boys present there (including me) became troubled. We packed up the game, left J to his home, didn't seem like big of a trouble. We didn't told our mumma anything and went for sleep. Suddenly I wake up on 11 Pm and saw that police is outside my home and fuckin case is filed against my father and brother for beating J inhumanly with rods. J’s mother (let's call her S) was shouting outside our home. My father wasn't present in the city itself that time, he used to do the servicing of photocopy machines. He was in another city that day for the same purpose. He came at night, 10 PM. You know what? There were 8–10 boys playing with us, they didn't even helped us and said they were not playing there. No one from the area supported us, everyone was just playing with us, their parents asked them to stay from police related things. Things went against us, we were saying exactly opposite of what entire area was saying, they were lying to prevent themselves from getting involved. My father has to spend one day in the police station (not behind bars). Also, since he was in another city, nothing big happened. Police also started knowing that the case was fake. Because beating badly will damage multiple body parts, but it was just shoulder dislocation type thing. J’s family was saying my brother and father broke his arm. They made fake documents for the case (You will realise later how we knew). We couldn't do anything. We offered J full treatment, everything from our side, but they declined. We realised what they wanted… We started doing talks with J’s family to end up things silently without going to court. We did negotiations and finally things ended up paying ₹70k to J’s family and ₹2.5k to the police. And the case was closed. And guess what, J didn't ever wear a plaster cuz It was all fake reports and all. Story ended? What do you think? Well no…. actual shit starts here.. From this event, they did similar things with many other people, fake rape cases for J’s sister, and all bullshit and taking money for dissolving the case. They started selling alcohol and drugs on a big scale, all this just 100m away from my home. They were earning big, enjoying life, buying out news vehicles every month, buying out properties and everything. Untill Karma started chasing them, they got in legal trouble, J died in a car accident, J’s mother and father both started going jail and court everyday, J’s sister hanged herself due to depression. Entire family collapsed, it was 2013 when they scammed my family, It was 2018 when J died in car accident. It was 2019 beginning when they started going jail everyday, It was 2019 end, when J’s sister suicide. After this incident, me and my brother started taking academics more seriously, stopped going near the area, stopped everything. My mom didn't let us going there, obviously, we stopped interacting with those shitty neighbours who didn't support us. We remembered their statement that hamara ladka toh uss time padh raha tha… I forget to share 1 thing, when my brother was in class Nur to 2. J and him were best friends. My mom and J’s mom were befriended too (since dono ke bachche same class me same school me the). ~ A story worth making a movie. Maybe once you'll see, I swear… It's in my list. ~ Wounds might have healed from this event, but marks are still there. ~ trying to live a life worth remembering

Dog was running at an angle, to protect myself, I started increasing the speed and running away from it. The divider on the roads were not that big, they were of about 12cm height. [Everything was going fast paced that time] Dog came very close to me and Suddenly, I realised I had 2 choices, either hit that dog or get to other (wrong) side by crossing the divider. (Hope you understood with this image) I decided the divider plan. My front tire hit the divider… ——————————-I don't know what happened—————————— (I believe that my head made the first impact with the floor..) I was standing on my feet, a completely random person with his bike (I don't remember bike name)on the other side of divider, my cycle was down (I don't remember what I felt about it that moment). The guy was asking me to sit on his bike and he'll drop me at hospital. I denied and said, mai akela chala jaunga He insisted, 2 of my classmates were on the footpath and said ki Bhai hospital chala ja. I was in some another state that time and repeated multiple times, Mai khud chala jaunga, aap jao Finally, on their multiple requests, I asked one of the 2 guys to have my cycle. On the bike, I realised lot of blood falling from my arm to my trouser, I took handkerchief (hanki in short) and putted in the arm, entire hanki became red in no time. I was able to see my knee bleeding. Then I realised the Bike MF is going out of campus (the hospital out of campus is shit expensive, but wait I have health insurance, so I got chill) I asked him to drop me at IIT hospital, he didn't listened and dropped me at Powai hospital (govt. hospital). He again clean my wounds, applied some stuff, he then picked some scissors and said Stitches lagenge I got tense, another doctor came, I got relaxed, he said Ghar pe boldo stitches nahi lagenge. and made a prescription for me Then we left for room. I planned to do study and some work on a project, but destiny have planned something else for me. I didn't do any work I planned. What if a car come from other side when I was hitting the divider, surely I wouldn't be writing this post? Ngl, that purple region still scares me, I know everything but I don't know the middle path. Question: Have you been scammed? What happened and what did you lose?
Answer: Just try to read this till the end, you’ll definitely learn very good lessons. Ok, this is around a 7–8 Yr. old story if i recall correctly, I was in class 6th or 7th that time. I was 11–12 years old at that time, my brother was 3 Yr. older than me… so, he was 14–15. Our family conditions weren’t financially that good, so we used to regularly look for opportunities to make some extra income. It was one day that we received some message on our phone about a job offer, offering some 1.5k-2k a day for some work related to MS office, It was work from home, they had some office in delhi. It sounds lucrative and we weren’t that educated those times, we told this to our mother. She agreed to call them and let us disscuss more about it. On the call, a lady picked up, she said “tumhe delhi me hamare office aana hoga, Rs. 2000 joining ke liye dene honge and laptop ki zarurat hogi kaam karne ke liye”. The offer sounds good, and it attracted us, obviously there weren't that much information regarding scams those days like it is today. We fell into it. My father income was very less to buy even an entry level laptop. So, My mother decided to sell some of her wedding jewellery to arrange the money, so that we both can study and also do the work. We got the laptop, my brother and mother travelled to Delhi, and got everything done. They gave us some work to do with MS office, which I can't recall right now, but we weren't able to do that. But now, we purchased the laptop which wasn't that useful for us, 7–8 yrs. ago, saari padhai copy books pe hoti thi na. Now guess what? Due to this scam, we got the laptop due to which (writing in order)… i) My mother's sister was doing her BioTech BSC but she didn't have money to get a laptop, my mom give that laptop to her so that she can complete her studies. She later returned it after doing her education, and then, ii) My brother cleared NEET, and got into medical college. He also did a lot of his studies with it. iii) then me, I cracked JEE Advanced using only that laptop (and 220 per month Vi recharge)😃 and got into IIT Bombay. Now, lesson? Question: What are some interesting IIT stories?
Answer: Story 1.. This story is actually of one of my friend (JEE Advanced AIR under 1000), he is in Mech. dept. here and is ofc a first year student. Let me name him A. He is one is those students who was studying regularly from the beginning. He was very good in maths, literally very good. Ask him any tutorial question, he'll tell you the solution before you could look for answer. We had a maths course in the first half of sem-1, MA109 namely. It was fuckin’ tough, ass breaking course, for CSE students too, literally very tough. Someday, we had a maths quiz and A taught me some concept the day before the quiz. We all went for quiz and he was very confident about it. And I was very nervous, literally thinking that…. We all give the quiz, and later realised he scored much less than us, literally one of the guys he taught entire stuff scored more than double than him. And guess what would had happened?… Quiz came out to be very easy than what we had expected, literally very easy, nothing incomparsion to tutorial questions, PYQs, everything. And guess what…. the girl had set A, while my friend A had the other. Even though question were similar, but they were not same. In some questions, only ordering was different. Now, what you expect from such IITian?…..He worked damn hard for MA109 midsem, literally more than anyone i personally know here. But now, paper turns out to be extremely tough. And this time, even CSE students seems to be struggling for 15 out of 30. Story 2 (Happened yesterday during Techfest Day 2).. One of my friend, let's name him B, is an organiser in Techfest, opposite to what the word ‘organiser’ sounds, being organiser is not a big deal, plus organisers have to work their ass off under coordinators (Post for 2nd year students) He was organiser in International Exhibition, when the event got over at 6 Pm, he got to help some foreigners with ATM. Those foreigners were pretty much interested in attending the flagship event of the night, ROBOWARS. They bind up all their exhibition things and decided to went for ROBOWARS, but they were late by 30 Min (due to IE) and It is a rule for ROBOWARS that nobody can enter after it gets started. They contacted my friend B, thinking that he have great powers and can get them to ROBOWARS, he took them to OAT gate and guess what…. On the gate, he told security that… Foreigners aaye hai, unhe andar jaana hai… And ofc hearing the word ‘foreigner’, they open gate for them in the middle of the event, plus my friend B also got to attend ROBOWARS in the light of foreigners… And foreigners still thinking that they got to ROBOWARS because of B, but the reality is he got to the event because of them😂 When he told us about the thing, we all laughed at him with the note, Foreigners Ko Chu**ya banaya. Answer: Kinda Mixed Feelings. But Definitely, Not As Great As One Expects. Me with my wingies (4 missing). I'm one in light blue t-shirt. idk how to begin, what to write, who'll read this and all those things. In this, I'm gonna share my first 15 days experience, here at IIT Bombay. • Classes, 🥲 Boring Af, Most of the time here, profs are not interested in teaching, even sometimes they don't address doubts of students. (Not all profs are like this btw) PS : If someone wants to know how much classes we have, this depends. I have around 25 hrs combining everything, lecs, labs and tuts. Result of such classes : We (atleast I) have a design course, what do you expect? Graphic Designing, Car designing (kucch zyada ho gaya ik) or maybe atleast some good stuff. But wait, what they are planning to teach? Prof told us, those students raise their hand who wants to design and stitch their convocation (event at the end of degree) scalf. idk what this means. We have CH105 course, common for every branch including BS Economics. Idk in which universe, a person related to economics will identify cis trans things in some big OC structures. • Culturals, lots of events happening! I'm not interested in watching some Bollywood stars standing in the crowd. But it can be good for some. So, i can't comment here. Img credit (Event organised this wednesday) : Vaishnav from mech dept. Last week, Katrina Kaif came here. Again, i was not interested. If you're interested in these things, I mean watching some heavily makeup stars, huh I've no words for you. • Sports, again lots of events happening. But. What we've heard : IITB has very big grounds. Credit : to this guy, Anish AJ. Reality : Yep, they have, I will not argue. But, You are not alone, there are 12k more folks to use them. Rest you know. They are really crowded when you got some time to play. When i say crowded, I mean it. H1 folks are lucky to have ground in their hostel. Some are staying at H16, have nothing except the partial Co-Ed ness of hostel. • Friends : Amazing, Depressing and Demotivating at the same time. This is one of the best things here, we enjoy,we play mini militia, gully cricket in our wing, late night talks, roasting one member of the group and many more things but… 1. Most of the people here are like all rounders, seeing them demotivates me. Ik the reason why they are such, but don't want to write here. Hard Work Beats Talent When Talent Does Not Work Hard. This is what we were taught. But what if talent do work hard, This is what happens in IIT Bombay. People here are good at everything you can imagine, even in swimming too, even in weightlifting too. I'm talking about freshers btw. I know you might be like ye banda sirf burai hi kar raha hai but this is what I've observed. • Mess Pic : Special Dinner (idk why they say this Gala dinner). Don't consider this as regular meal Atleast here I can say, mess is good taste-wise but their food, no matter what they cook, around 80–90% of time tastes same. But they don't try much permutation and combinations, which overall lowers the level of food. Overall, it's eatable. And, it's as good as you don't necessarily need to purchase food from some restaurant. One more thing i can't miss : daily they make one dish which we can't identify (atleast we, from north India) • Campus, You'll Find Couples Everywhere. Attaching Some Images. Big campuses sounds fun. But wait… is this fun to walk 2km from hostel room to lecture hall complex. Yep! if you've some great friends. H7 😂, Spooky I know, I don't have that much beautiful images. H16, Good In Every Aspect I can Judge. • Seniors, Here, there is literally no ragging. Seniors (ISMP Mentor to be more precise) infact give treats. This place is literally fun, demotivating, depressing, and every feeling you can imagine at the same time. My 15 stay day here have taught me 2 things here, never compare with others and follow what your heart says, not the herd. So, Thanks for reading this. And Maybe, I've told some not so good things about IITB. But it is what it is….. This is just my 15 day experience. I can't argue that I can be wrong at some places here but till now, it is what I've observed.

Question: Where did you get the full syllabus mock test?
Answer: Hi and Thanks For A2A (Ik I'm doing this after a long time) Just after I finished my JEE syllabus, I too had same problem. These are the resources i used. First of all, before coming to the list, please try to analyse mock tests carefully, it can literally boost your score a lot. Second, start giving full mocks at this stage no matter how much of your syllabus is completed. Marks doesn't matter, but experience and learnings do. 1. NTA Abhyaas Just after I completed my syllabus, I started giving my mock tests from NTA Abhyaas App. And believe me, they are very relevant when it comes to question level and etc. But 1 thing i noticed which I didn't liked is the weightage of chapters. You can too try them. One Thing : NTA Abhyaas App Is Developed By Embibe Not NTA. 2. Previous Year Papers What I did in my time was I didn't solved 2021 papers chapterwise instead I solved them as full papers at the end. Where You Can Solve = Allen TestMyPrep App 3. Allen Major Test Series Initially, I had no plans of spending on my JEE prep but when JM was postponed in April, I purchased Allen Major TS (had only full syllabus tests), they were very relevant and had mocks for Advanced too. Price = 1.5K Where You Can Buy = Allen TestMyPrep App (Not promoting but telling bc in one of my posts when I wrote about the same, students have same query there.) 4. Mathongo AYJR Not a test series but only 1 test conducted just 1 week before actual JEE Mains. IDK why but I think it is worth mentioning here. That's it, these were the tests I gave during my JEE preparation. And 1 more thing I'd like to add here, do not give mocks in hope to get same questions in the exam, instead give them to learn from your mistakes. And do analyse mock, without it, mock test ka koi matlab hi nahi hai. All the best.
